title: Teaching the press roll and why George banned drum solos
summary: Young drummers cannot make a press roll; Lewis told him to cut the fancy solos because they throw the band off.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Jazz is over there to stay. On the other side. But they're taking more of the jazz than anything else. Everywhere we went over there there was a jazz group. And now you take these college... American college boys. Every college you go to... Has got a little jazz group. All of them. The reason why I know that... Because everyone that we played a concert... They invited us out to a little gathering they had... And they had their little jazz groups to entertain us. And they're trying to play authentic jazz. See? But what they want to... What the most important thing they're trying to get together is the beat. That's what they want is the beat. That's what they want is the beat. And that's what I've been trying to teach them many of them. Because they'd all come and say, How you do this, how you do that, how you do the other. And I would take time during intermission and show them. See? Now I met a fellow one night in... Indianapolis. Youngster. Was playing with a 14-piece orchestra. When I was... And I was backstage. And Gary Nash and Simmons said, He said, How do you make a press roll? I said, Who you playing with? He said, I'm playing with... This 14-piece outfit. And I said to myself, He's playing with a 14-piece outfit And I don't know how to make a press roll. I found it strange. You know? I see a press roll is easy.
But a lot of them can't do it. I don't care who they are.

That goes for... What's this white drummer's name there? Caught with Dope. Oh... You can know him if I could call his name. Uh-huh. Gene Krupa? Yeah, Gene Krupa. You take this fellow Rich. All them fellas, they do all that stuff. They don't forgot how you make a press roll. You know what I mean? The press roll is just going out of their mind. All they want to do is just work on that stuff in front of them. Now you don't call them jazz drummers. They don't think how they make a press roll. No. They don't think how they make a press roll. See? Because all they want to do is just a solo. George told me one day, he said, Joe, you see all that you doing there on taking a solo? He said, you cut it out. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. He said, you cut it out. He said, it's alright to make an explosion because some of the numbers call for it. But he said, you try to stay off all that fancy stuff. He said, I'm going to tell you why. You're going to throw the band off. You're going to either increase or you're going to fall. And he didn't lie. But I listened to many of them drummers on TV taking solos and bands who hardly know where they exactly come in. Unless somebody just concentrating hard on how the numbers going, you understand, when they're supposed to come in and they're following behind him. So I just made up my mind to give it up.
